correctness.rationale: For all strictly positive model parameters satisfying resident nonbalance, a=d(Q1/P1-Q2/P2) is nonzero. The invader-at-resident transverse determinant is -a²/(Q1Q2), so exactly one positive real eigenvalue exists. At the unique invader-only profile the normalized component order t1>t2 and t1>1 yields a strictly positive resident-invasion determinant and negative trace; both tangential scalar blocks are Hurwitz by a scaling comparison and Metzler criterion. The no-coexistence argument uses conserved patch fluxes, proportionality in two dimensions, and the negative coefficient in m=alpha P+beta Q. All quantifiers, nonnegative boundary cases and rigorous equalities appear in RESULT.md. verify.py reproduces the exact rational example using actual decoded files; no numerical test substitutes for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: A literature-led finite-patch theorem addresses an explicitly stated identical-resource stationary-mimicry question in arXiv:2512.10898v1. That source proves success under strictly higher resources, not the tested equal-resource case. Earlier Lou two-patch results use equal intrinsic growth with K-dependent crowding; Chen et al. uses one common dispersal matrix. Searches and full-text implication comparisons did not find the combined universal two-patch theorem, but broader historical criteria may exist. The equal-intrinsic-growth subfamily overlaps known ideal-free competition results, so originality is claimed for the simultaneous heterogeneous-intrinsic-rate, distinct-target classification, not for the homogeneous special case.
residual_risks: Theorem is deliberately local/equilibrium only and does not settle global competitive exclusion or the PDE conjecture.
Uninspected specialist two-patch evolutionary-dispersal papers or broader theorems may imply the special case through a nonobvious transformation or criterion.
The 2019 Lou survey contains a very close structural two-patch classification for a different local logistic law, and independent novelty verification is still warranted.

Qi–Su–Wang (2024) and Chen–Liu–Wu (2022) are plausible specialist two-patch papers whose full theorems were not accessible during this review; abstracts do not establish a decisive implication but novelty may be affected.

value.rationale: The source expressly asks whether invasion and exclusion remain possible when resident and invader share resources and the invader mimics the resident stationary distribution. On a natural irreducible two-patch discrete analogue, the theorem answers three precise quantitative structural questions for every positive invader dispersal rate: strictly positive invasion eigenvalue, invader-only local attracting equilibrium, and no positive coexistence stationary state. Exact cancellation in a determinant and a conservation/proportionality obstruction are substantive explanations, not a small numerical parameter gain. Explicit limits avoid treating local attraction as global elimination.
